input: The adsorption of a dye from water onto activated carbon was investigated by means of batch tests carried out at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was found to be 237 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. At an adsorbent dose of 1.1 g L-1, the removal achieved after 120 min corresponded to 85% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. It is important to note that the capacity is a fit parameter derived from applying the Langmuir equation to the batch data, and that it is reported for pH 5 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured, so the figure cannot be assumed to extend across the pH range. Removal, meanwhile, is stated relative to the initial concentration: at the stated dose and contact time, the carbon successfully took up 85% of the dye that was present at the outset of the test. The two figures ultimately rest on quite different bases. Capacity is a property of the adsorbent under the fit, expressed per gram, whereas removal is the outcome of a single test conducted at one dose and one contact time, and a higher dose or a longer contact time would inevitably change it. Both figures are stated for the specific conditions tested, namely at 298 K and pH 5, and neither should be carried across to other temperatures, other doses, or other initial concentrations.
